name: Pork Pot Pie
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
steps: Prepare pie crusts as directed on package for two-crust pie using 9-inch pie pan.
In a medium saucepan, melt margarine over medium heat.
Add onion; cook 2 minutes or until tender.
Stir in flour, salt, and pepper until well-blended.
Gradually stir in broth and milk; cook, stirring constantly, until bubbly and thickened.
Add pork, corn, and peas; remove from heat.
Spoon pork mixture into crust-lined pan.
Top with second crust and flute; cut three slits on top.
Bake for 30–40 minutes or until crust is golden-brown.

culture.text: A pot pie or potpie is a type of savory pie that is popular in the United States. It is usually a meat pie, covered by a pie crust consisting of flaky pastry. Pot pies may be made with a variety of fillings, including poultry, beef, seafood or plant-based meat substitute fillings, and may also differ in the types of crust. The name is chiefly used in America.
